summary: The design’s main gap is that the existing build CLI cannot place its plane outside the clone as described: it derives storage from repository config and writes configuration and build artifacts back into the clone. The highest risks are cross-worker locking, branch/authentication correctness, subprocess lifetime, partial-plane failure, and exposing the mutating wiki toolkit to the reviewer LLM.

suggestions.title: Make external storage an explicit build input
suggestions.rationale: `wikitoolkit build --path` resolves `config.storage_path(root)`, defaults to `<root>/.parrot/wiki`, persists `.parrot/wiki.json`, and writes build reports/README/export artifacts. The proposed absolute `storage_dir` cannot be supplied by the documented command alone; add an explicit storage override or a dedicated build API before implementing reviewer wiring.

suggestions.title: Use a lock shared across reviewer instances and gunicorn workers
suggestions.rationale: An `asyncio.Lock` would only serialize coroutines in one reviewer/process. Gunicorn workers and multiple reviewer instances can concurrently pull the same clone, while `wiki_write_lock` protects only the plane. The clone refresh and build need a process-shared repository lock, or a single app-level repository manager.

suggestions.title: Validate the cached clone’s remote and checked-out branch
suggestions.rationale: `clone_repo` treats any directory containing `.git` as the correct cache and delegates to `pull_repo`. `pull_repo(..., branch=...)` runs `git pull origin <branch>` but does not check out or verify that branch, so a reused cache can build the wrong repository or merge the base branch into the wrong local branch.

suggestions.title: Do not let incidental `gh` availability break private authentication
suggestions.rationale: Private cloning prefers `gh repo clone` whenever the binary exists, but that path does not use the PAT or GitHub App token held by `GitToolkit`. A deployed process may have `gh` installed but unauthenticated, and App installation tokens are not automatically available to `gh`; require explicit authentication or fall back to token-authenticated git.

suggestions.title: Implement cancellable subprocess timeouts
suggestions.rationale: `GitToolkit._run_subprocess` awaits `communicate()` without a timeout. The open build-timeout setting therefore cannot prevent a hung git/build process from blocking a PR review. The runner must terminate and reap the child on timeout, and distinguish timeout degradation from ordinary build failure.

suggestions.title: Preserve a last-known-good plane on failed refreshes
suggestions.rationale: The build acquires a writer lock but ingests and exports incrementally before completion; an exception can leave a partially updated SQLite plane. “Fall back to diff-only” is not sufficient if the reviewer has already attached that partial plane. Build into a generation or validate-and-publish location, or explicitly mark the prior plane unusable until a complete build succeeds.

suggestions.title: Treat the full LLM wiki surface as a mutation capability
suggestions.rationale: `LLMWikiToolkit` exposes `create_page`, `update_page`, `delete_page`, `remember`, ingestion, and export operations; `confine_sources` defaults to `False`. Attaching the complete toolkit gives a PR-review LLM write and path-sensitive capabilities, not merely repository lookup. Require explicit capability gating or a read-only registration surface, even if unrestricted namespaces remain an owner-approved option.

suggestions.title: Canonicalize repository identity before enrichment
suggestions.rationale: Webhook handling checks the repository, but public `review_pull_request` accepts a payload repository and the existing GitToolkit accepts raw slugs and URLs. Enrichment should always use the configured `self.repository` after canonical validation, otherwise a manually triggered payload can select another clone/cache and credential scope.

suggestions.title: Resolve the `dev` versus `main` branch contract explicitly
suggestions.rationale: The accepted flow requires `base_branch: dev`, while `_build_git_toolkit()` defaults `GIT_DEFAULT_BRANCH` to `main` and `GitToolkit` also defaults to `main`. The feature needs a dedicated, validated base-branch setting and tests proving both initial clone and refresh operate on `dev`; the prompt should report that exact snapshot branch.

suggestions.title: Bound and label injected wiki context
suggestions.rationale: `_ask_llm_for_review()` currently builds a fixed ticket/diff prompt, while `DevLoopWikiSearch` demonstrates bounded `pack_results` context injection. The new block needs a hard token budget and labels such as “base-branch snapshot; PR-added symbols may be absent,” otherwise the full tool schemas plus ranked context can crowd out the diff or cause false nonexistent-symbol findings.

suggestions.title: Add deterministic degradation and lifecycle tests
suggestions.rationale: Existing reviewer tests cover mocked diff/tool-call behavior and toolkit registration, while clone tests cover subprocess argv/token scrubbing. The feature needs tests for fresh and reused `dev` clones, private PAT/App authentication, concurrent same-repo events, build nonzero exit/timeout, absent or partial planes, warm-up cancellation, and continued diff-only review after each failure.

suggestions.title: Own and cancel warm-up tasks explicitly
suggestions.rationale: `post_configure()` currently performs awaited wiring but has no repository-enrichment task ownership or shutdown hook. A background build must be stored, deduplicated, logged, and cancelled/awaited during app shutdown; otherwise reloads can leave orphaned subprocesses and unobserved task exceptions while startup appears healthy.
